entry.title: UK AI Startup 22one Reaches Nearly $400M Valuation in Funding Round Backed by Sequoia and Lux
entry.content:
Links: ft.com

UK stealth artificial intelligence startup 22one has attained a valuation of nearly $400 million following a funding round backed by prominent venture capital firms including Sequoia Capital and Lux Capital. Founded by former Merseyside police officer Steven Richardson, the company is developing specialized artificial intelligence tools and services for law enforcement agencies and police forces.

Despite operating largely in stealth mode with minimal public visibility, the startup has attracted substantial investment from major Silicon Valley backers. The high valuation highlights growing venture capital interest in applying advanced artificial intelligence technologies to public sector security and operational workflows.

entry.title: Nvidia Backs Indian AI Startup Simplismart in $14 Million Series B Round
entry.content:
Links: techcrunch.com

Nvidia has participated in a $14 million Series B funding round for Bengaluru-based AI startup Simplismart, valuing the company at approximately $100 million. Dallas Venture Capital led the investment, with additional participation from Accel, Shastra VC, and Micromax. Simplismart develops software that sits between AI models and underlying computing infrastructure, automatically configuring deployments to balance speed, cost, and GPU utilization for enterprise customers.

The startup’s platform helps businesses optimize performance and reduce GPU serving costs, with clients including video-generation platforms InVideo and HeyGen. Simplismart has experienced rapid growth, scaling its annualized revenue run rate 14-fold over a six-month period and generating more than half its revenue from the United States. Alongside the funding, Nvidia is collaborating with Simplismart on technical integrations involving its Dynamo inference software to expand market adoption.

entry.title: Intel to Acquire Israeli Quantum Computing Startup Classiq
entry.content:
Links: bloomberg.com | source | hacker news

Intel Corp. has agreed to acquire Tel Aviv-based Classiq Technologies Ltd., a quantum computing software startup, to accelerate the development of a full-stack quantum computing platform. The acquisition aims to integrate Classiq's quantum algorithm synthesis platform with Intel's spin-qubit manufacturing and existing software capabilities.

The deal is estimated to be valued between $2.2 billion and $2.3 billion, representing one of the largest acquisitions in the quantum computing sector. Classiq has raised more than $200 million in funding and maintains a workforce of approximately 130 employees.

entry.title: California Startups Surpass Prior US Annual Funding Records in 2026
entry.content:
Links: news.crunchbase.com

California-based startups have secured more than three-fourths of all U.S. venture funding in 2026, pulling in an unprecedented $385 billion across seed- through growth-stage rounds. This figure exceeds the total amount raised by all U.S. startups in any prior single year on record, driven largely by massive megarounds for artificial intelligence pioneers based in San Francisco.

Major financing rounds for companies like OpenAI and Anthropic account for more than half of the statewide total, while other substantial contributions come from mature firms such as Waymo and Databricks as well as newer ventures like Prometheus and Safe Superintelligence. Additionally, early- and seed-stage California companies have captured nearly $62 billion, representing about 57% of all U.S. early-stage funding this year.

entry.title: Blackstone-Led CoreWeave Loan Sparks Chip-Backed Debt Boom
entry.content:
Links: bloomberg.com

A 2023 private credit loan of $2.3 billion led by Blackstone Inc. to CoreWeave Inc. established a model for financing artificial intelligence infrastructure using graphics processing units as collateral. This strategy has catalyzed a rapidly expanding chip-backed debt market projected to approach $1 trillion.

The initial financing arrangement has reshaped modern corporate credit by demonstrating how specialized tech assets can secure massive debt facilities. As lenders and borrowers continue to scale these GPU-backed facilities, the trend is introducing new risk profiles and transforming how capital is deployed across the tech sector.

entry.title: Taler Operations AG Founded to Operate GNU Taler in Germany
entry.content:
Links: taler.net | hacker news

Taler Operations AG is being established in Bochum, Germany, to operate the privacy-focused GNU Taler payment system in Euros. The newly formed company will apply to BaFin, the German financial supervisory authority, for an electronic money institution licence after the project's initial banking partner, GLS Bank, decided not to pursue the role.

GNU Taler remains free and open-source software, with the new corporate entity focusing strictly on managing the regulated payment infrastructure. To satisfy regulatory capital mandates and fund operations prior to revenue generation, Taler Operations AG is currently seeking investments of at least €50,000 from backers aligned with the project's privacy and public-interest goals.

entry.title: Microsoft and Alphabet Object to Tokenized Stock Trading on OKXICE Platform
entry.content:
Links: fortune.com

Microsoft and Alphabet have joined 14 other public companies in formally objecting to a plan by OKXICE—a joint venture between crypto exchange OKX and NYSE parent ICE—to offer round-the-clock tokenized trading of their shares. The companies utilized a Securities and Exchange Commission framework that allows qualifying firms to block third-party tokenized stock listings within a 30-day notice period.

The pushback highlights growing corporate caution toward digital asset trading, driven by concerns over potential pricing discrepancies and the loss of traditional market closures used for digesting earnings reports. While individual companies can block their shares from specific platforms using the regulatory exemption, the mounting objections threaten to strip the planned venture of a significant portion of its initial stock lineup.
